note: Reviewed lessons from past Factory attempts. Builder and reviewer lessons are added to every task contract at preparation; author lessons guide whoever writes task contracts. New lessons are proposed from attempt evidence and merged only through owner-approved pull requests.

lessons.text: If an exported type or signature you need is shown in the supplied files or quoted in the requirements, use it exactly; escalate only when something you must use is neither shown nor quoted.
Import local TypeScript modules that Node tests load with the explicit .ts extension (for example ./ai-cover.ts).
Keep repairs minimal: change only what the findings or failing checks require and return complete files only for paths you change.
Do not pass process.env directly where a narrow typed environment object is expected; copy the named variables into a plain object.
DynamoDB condition expressions cannot test whether a number is an integer; value-type checks belong in the pure availability function, and the condition enforces the comparisons.

Judge the proposal against the stated contract and acceptance tests. Do not reject for validation that is stricter or looser than the contract specifies; report a contract ambiguity as a finding only when it makes the specified behaviour unsafe.
Reference-only files (allowed but not required to change) must not be modified.
Change an existing file with several small anchored edits (each old_text occurs exactly once at that point; edits to one file apply in order) instead of one large replacement.

lessons.evidence: library-helpers-001 (gpt-6.1-terra) rejected twice for missing check output
lessons.text: You are asked to review only after the fixed sandbox command (typegen, tsc --noEmit, eslint and every repository and acceptance test) exited successfully; the stdout/stderr digests are its receipt. Do not reject for lack of check output. Judge the change against the contract and the code shown.
Measure the implementation turn with the delivery block and lessons included; tests/test_task_fit.py enforces the limits from recorded source sizes.
Show every module whose exports the new code uses, or quote the exact signatures in the requirements.
Every acceptance clause must be satisfiable for all valid inputs (a title can legitimately appear more than once in a prompt).
Check acceptance tests with deliberate mutants; a mutant that survives means a missing assertion.
Any manual reset or retry path must account for every side effect of the first attempt (records, stored files, reservations); prefer unique per-attempt names over deterministic ones.
Keep each task's output small: prefer new files over anchored edits of large or minified files, and split a component from its wiring into separate tasks.
